explanation.surface: A political spin doctor allied to the Liberals takes a radical stance in a play by Caryl Churchill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' turns the doctoring verb round to GIR, and 'revolutionary' does the same to the position. Churchill is the dramatist Caryl Churchill, not Winston, though the political surface points to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Girls is a 1982 play by the British dramatist Caryl Churchill, much concerned with Thatcher-era politics and women's careers.

clue.text: Mess or germ — topic difficult for a lady with OCD?

indicators.note: to mess something up is to jumble it, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mess or germs is a hard subject for a person obsessed with cleanliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' rearranges OR GERM TOPIC into OGMOREPRITC; add HARD. Mrs Ogmore-Pritchard, in Dylan Thomas's Under Milk Wood, is obsessed with cleanliness and makes even the sun wipe its shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas's Mrs Ogmore-Pritchard, of Under Milk Wood, is a fanatically house-proud widow, hence the question mark for a modern diagnosis.

clue.text: Three notes about one composer

explanation.surface: A simple description of a composer built from a few notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The notes are G, RE and G; 'about' wraps them round I (one), which lands between R and E. Edvard Grieg was the Norwegian composer of Peer Gynt.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Grieg was a Norwegian Romantic composer, famous for the Peer Gynt suites and his Piano Concerto.

clue.text: Strange lair in which a superior man met a very posh lady who wrote about nuns

explanation.definitionFit: Rumer Godden, the English novelist, wrote Black Narcissus and In This House of Brede, both set among communities of religious sisters.

clue.text: Ancient sorceress adopting core of plan to serve up raw seafood

clue.text: Lady in Ecclesiastes, the rudest book of the bible

clue.text: Bear's story included in video novel

clue.text: Wild savage drowned, or Lucy's lover who died in an improbable way

explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Ravenswood is the hero of Walter Scott's The Bride of Lammermoor, who loves Lucy Ashton and is swallowed by quicksand.

clue.text: Trollope's most important title of all?

definitions.meaning: the Duke of this name is the grandest peer in Trollope's Palliser novels
the Latin word meaning of all, as in a bus once called an omnibus, for all

explanation.surface: Asks which of Trollope's books or titles matters most of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Omnium is Plantagenet Palliser's title in Trollope's political novels; the Latin genitive plural means 'of all', so the duke's title literally says he is lord of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's Duke of Omnium is the richest, highest peer in his fiction, and the Latin genitive plural means belonging to everyone.

clue.text: End in sight in vegan fresh fruit harvest

explanation.definitionFit: Vendange is the French word, used in English, for the grape harvest or vintage.

clue.text: Reformed prisoner's scratched out message received previously

explanation.surface: A convict who went straight scratched out a message he had had earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the scratched letters into SCATCHERD. In Trollope's Doctor Thorne, Roger Scatcherd is a stonemason jailed for manslaughter who becomes a rich railway contractor and baronet.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's Roger Scatcherd serves a sentence for killing a man, then rises to become a wealthy contractor and baronet.

explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the see-plus-gossip pair into ANATOPS. Ana is a crossword favourite for gossip. William Cullen Bryant's poem on death ends with lying down 'to pleasant dreams'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanatopsis is William Cullen Bryant's meditation on death, whose last line ends 'and lies down to pleasant dreams'.
